transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because the clinic got on me about how little I've been eating lately. But honestly, most days I'm just grabbing a coffee before my shift at the warehouse, and maybe I'll have a yogurt or just a few bites of something after my GED class. It's just... sitting down for a real meal, it feels like it throws off everything I'm trying to keep in line. So they told me I needed to come in and talk to someone.
How long have you been eating this way, with little food most days?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's been a while, I guess. I didn't really keep track of when it started being like this every day. It just kind of became my normal routine somewhere along the way.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently, or do you have concerns about gaining weight?

Well, I definitely have concerns about gaining weight. If I eat something heavy, like... I don't know, fried food from the break room at work, or a big plate of food at church, I get really scared it’s going to show on me right away. I'll just keep thinking about it, and I usually want to go check the scale just to make sure.
After eating, do you ever make yourself sick or do anything else to try to prevent gaining weight, like using laxatives or exercising a lot more than usual?

No, I don't do anything like that. I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything. And I'm on my feet packing boxes all day at work, so I don't really have the energy to go exercise a bunch after my shift anyway. I mostly just... try to avoid eating too much in the first place so I don't have to worry about it.
Do you ever find yourself eating a lot more than usual in a short amount of time, like feeling like you've lost control over how much you're eating?

No, not really. I don't ever just... lose control and eat a huge amount of food all at once. Like I said before, I mostly just try to keep what I eat to a minimum, so I don't really have times where I overdo it like that.
Do you judge yourself mainly based on your body weight or shape, or do you feel that they are really important to how you see yourself?

Yeah, I guess I do. It's really important to how I see myself. When I look in the mirror, like before work or going to play softball, my stomach and my thighs still look a lot bigger than they should. 

Honestly, what I see right then kind of dictates everything. It can make me feel like I’m either doing good or just completely failing for the whole day.
How much does your fear of gaining weight or concern about your body shape affect your daily life, like your ability to focus, your mood, or how you spend your time?

Well, it affects things a fair amount, I guess. I mean, I'm still showing up for work every day, and I go to my GED classes. But... I've actually been leaving my homework unfinished lately. It's just hard to concentrate on it when my mind is so focused on keeping my eating and my whole schedule totally controlled. 

And it changes how I spend my time, too. Like, I've been turning down meals with people after church because I just need to stick to my routine and not mess up. So, yeah, it definitely takes up a lot of my mental energy and gets in the way of normal stuff.
When you choose to eat very little, is it mainly because you're trying to lose weight or keep from gaining it, or is it more about other reasons like the way food looks, tastes, or feels?

It's definitely about the weight. I don't really have an issue with how food tastes or feels... I mean, I like food just fine. It's really just because I'm trying to lose weight, or, you know, at least make sure I don't gain any. That's the only reason I keep what I eat to a minimum. It doesn't have anything to do with textures or anything like that.
When you think about your weight or body shape, do you experience it differently than what others might say, like seeing yourself as larger even if others don't comment on your weight?

Yeah, I think so. It's kind of like what I was mentioning earlier... when I look in the mirror before my GED class or before softball, my stomach and my thighs just still look bigger than they should. 

Other people don't really comment on it or say I look big, but that's what I see when I look at myself. And depending on what I see right then, it makes me feel like I'm either doing good or just completely failing for the whole day. So, yeah, I guess I do see it differently than others might.
Have you ever reached a point where you were so focused on controlling your eating and weight that you lost a significant amount of weight, or came close to being underweight?

Yeah, I have. I mean, I've lost enough that my work pants are pretty loose on me now, and some people have actually told me I look too thin. But honestly, when I step on the scale and see that number go down, it just feels like I'm finally getting somewhere. I know people think I'm underweight or whatever, but I really don't see why I should be pushed to put the weight back on when I'm finally making progress.

When you look at yourself and feel like you need to lose more weight, is it because you feel like you haven't reached a weight or shape you were aiming for, or is it more about how you see yourself in the mirror not matching how you want to feel about your body?

I guess it's a bit of both, but mostly it's about what I see in the mirror. I mean, I have a number in my head that I'd like to reach, but even when the scale goes down, I look at my stomach or my thighs and they just don't look right to me yet. It's like... what I see doesn't match how I want to look, so I just feel like I need to keep going until it does.
